housing: North Warwickshire is a largely rural borough of market towns and former mining villages, with Atherstone, Coleshill and Polesworth the largest settlements. Much of the housing is semis, bungalows and post-war council-built estates, with brick terraces in the old colliery villages and period cottages in the countryside. Private renting is a modest share of homes, and new-build estates have grown near the M42 at Dordon and Polesworth.
checkinTips: Former colliery terraces in Polesworth, Arley and Dordon: photograph damp at the base of walls, back yards and outbuildings.
Period houses on Atherstone's Long Street and in Coleshill: record sash windows, old doors, uneven floors and any cellar.
Rural cottages and farm lets: photograph oil tanks, septic tanks or cesspits, stoves and chimneys, and note the fuel level.
New-build estates near the M42: photograph snagging marks, sealant, and the state of turf and fences.
Bungalows let to older tenants: note grab rails, ramps and any adaptations, and their condition.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in privately rented homes to North Warwickshire Borough Council's private sector housing team.
